articles.article_title: The Axiom of the Biospheric Commons
articles.chapter_title: THE PREAMBLE & THE INVARIANT BILL OF RIGHTS

qa.q: Who does the planet's air, water, soil and shared knowledge belong to?
qa.a: All living beings, together. It is an indivisible commons, not something anyone can split up and own.

qa.q: Can anyone buy it, sell it or fence it off?
qa.a: No. It cannot become private speculative property, be used for unearned financial gain, or be closed off by a state's territorial claim.

qa.q: Can I own land or other resources?
qa.a: Only as a right to use them, and only while you actually occupy them, take care of them, and keep them intact for future generations.

articles.article_title: Invariant Personal and Bodily Sovereignty
articles.chapter_title: THE PREAMBLE & THE INVARIANT BILL OF RIGHTS

qa.q: Who controls my body and mind?
qa.a: You do. Every person has absolute, unconditional control over their own body and mind, including their privacy and the right to a compassionate, freely chosen death.

qa.q: What can never be done to me?
qa.a: Forced genetic changes, tracking of your body data without your consent, monitoring of your brain, drugging you against your will, and physical domination are permanently banned.

qa.q: Can an emergency or a government order override this?
qa.a: No. No public mandate, collective emergency, or official decree may violate your body or mind.

articles.article_title: The Universal Baseline of Survival
articles.chapter_title: THE PREAMBLE & THE INVARIANT BILL OF RIGHTS

qa.q: Do I have to work to get food, water and a home?
qa.a: No. Basic life support is a birthright for every inhabitant, not tied to work, buying, debt or agreeing with any ideology.

qa.q: What does basic life support cover?
qa.a: Clean water, enough food, safe housing, full healthcare including prevention and emergencies, energy for heating, cooling and cooking, and open access to knowledge, culture and basic tools.

qa.q: Can a group take these away to make me behave or work?
qa.a: No. No assembly, institution or group may use survival as a tool to control behavior, extract labor or punish.

articles.article_title: Invariant Civil Liberties and Epistemic Freedom
articles.chapter_title: THE PREAMBLE & THE INVARIANT BILL OF RIGHTS

qa.q: What freedoms do I have?
qa.a: Unconditional freedom of thought, conscience, speech, peaceful assembly, voluntary association and cultural expression, for every person and group.

qa.q: Can anyone silence views that others dislike?
qa.a: No. Councils, assemblies and digital systems may not censor peaceful dissent, suppress unconventional questions, or require people to hold an approved belief.

qa.q: Is there space for unconventional research?
qa.a: Yes. Seven percent (7%) of shared fabrication facilities, computing capacity and laboratories is permanently reserved for speculative research, without review by peers. Research on deadly engineered pathogens, mass nerve agents or radiological weapons is banned, and lab machines carry public, tamper-evident locks that block dangerous sequences.

qa.q: What if more people apply than there is room for?
qa.a: Access is given by a transparent rotating lottery among applicants, with no screening of their ideas.

articles.article_title: The Anti-Enclosure Principle
articles.chapter_title: THE PREAMBLE & THE INVARIANT BILL OF RIGHTS

qa.q: Can a contract or title let someone take back control of things people need to live?
qa.a: No. Any title, contract or administrative device that does this, brings back landlords who profit from homes they do not live in, or exploits control of necessities to charge for them is void.

qa.q: Can anyone own a patent on a scientific discovery or a tool design?
qa.a: No. Discoveries, genetics, algorithms and tool designs are public goods, permanently free of patents, intellectual property claims and proprietary restrictions.

articles.article_title: Ecological Duty and Intergenerational Stewardship
articles.chapter_title: THE PREAMBLE & THE INVARIANT BILL OF RIGHTS

qa.q: What do I owe the environment?
qa.a: Everyone who uses shared planetary resources must look after nature. Human life must stay within what local river basins and the whole biosphere can renew and support.

qa.q: What environmental harm counts as a crime?
qa.a: Deliberately poisoning ecosystems, using up underground water reserves that do not refill, and destroying habitats beyond repair are crimes against planetary continuity.

qa.q: Can nature itself have a voice in law?
qa.a: Yes. Living things other than humans, and whole natural regions, have rights in law. Human guardians chosen by lot defend them before civic assemblies.

articles.article_title: Primacy and Inviolability of Fundamental Rights
articles.chapter_title: THE PREAMBLE & THE INVARIANT BILL OF RIGHTS

qa.q: Can the rights in this chapter ever be taken away?
qa.a: No. They are fixed parts of the constitution that no one can remove or weaken.

qa.q: Can a vote or an emergency override them?
qa.a: No. No assembly, referendum, state of emergency or large majority vote can suspend, reduce or give up these rights. Anything contrary to them is void from the start.

articles.article_title: Abolition of Absentee Title and the Deconstruction of Dominium
articles.chapter_title: PROPERTY DECONSTRUCTION & THE JURISPRUDENCE OF USUFRUCT

qa.q: Can I own land or property outright?
qa.a: No. Absolute private ownership is abolished. You hold land, water, farmland, natural areas and factory machinery only as a conditional right, based on actually using them, being present and caring for them.

qa.q: What happens to property I leave empty or hold just to sell later?
qa.a: It goes straight back to the local commons. Ownership without active use is treated as not existing.

articles.article_title: The Tripartite Classification of Goods and Commons
articles.chapter_title: PROPERTY DECONSTRUCTION & THE JURISPRUDENCE OF USUFRUCT

qa.q: Can anyone take my personal belongings?
qa.a: No. Your clothes, furnishings, art, intimate items, craft tools and personal computing devices stay yours permanently. No civic assembly can take or reassign them. Spare duplicate tools are not protected in this way.

qa.q: Can I lose my home to a landlord or a bank?
qa.a: No. A home, plot or small workshop you live in and maintain can never be foreclosed, and no one can charge you rent for it. The people living there with you can take over the right to stay.

qa.q: Who runs things like water, forests, hospitals and power grids?
qa.a: Local councils of citizens chosen by lot and dedicated work groups run them. They are shared, cannot be divided, and are held in trust for current and future generations.

articles.article_title: Inalienable Housing Security and the Absolute Ban on Eviction
articles.chapter_title: PROPERTY DECONSTRUCTION & THE JURISPRUDENCE OF USUFRUCT

qa.q: Can I be evicted from my home?
qa.a: No. Being evicted or displaced into homelessness or destitution is unconstitutional, and secure housing is a right that cannot be taken away.

qa.q: Can a landlord charge me rent?
qa.a: No. Renting out homes for money and holding property for speculation are legally void.

qa.q: Who decides if I must move because of a hazard or a domestic crisis?
qa.a: A Local Mediation Panel of three citizens chosen by lot settles disputes over relocation.

qa.q: When could I actually be made to move?
qa.a: Only after the community has secured an equal or better home that meets the needs of the people living there.

articles.article_title: Stewardship of Arable Soil and Productive Assets
articles.chapter_title: PROPERTY DECONSTRUCTION & THE JURISPRUDENCE OF USUFRUCT

qa.q: Can I buy or sell farmland?
qa.a: No. Farmland, the sea areas where young fish grow, and industrial plants can't be bought, sold, mortgaged or leased for money.

qa.q: Who gets farmland?
qa.a: Farming collectives, family farmers and farming trusts, based on the region's food needs and proven farming that restores the soil.

qa.q: How long can I keep my land?
qa.a: Across generations, as long as you keep the soil, water and wildlife healthy. If you keep poisoning it or stop farming, a regional assembly reviews the case and, if the breach is confirmed, the land passes to others willing to care for it.

articles.article_title: Common Heritage Sanctuaries and Positional Assets
articles.chapter_title: PROPERTY DECONSTRUCTION & THE JURISPRUDENCE OF USUFRUCT

qa.q: Can someone buy a beautiful natural spot, like a coastline or mountain ridge, for themselves?
qa.a: No. Unique or ecologically sensitive places such as headlands, riverbanks, alpine crests and historical sanctuaries can never be enclosed as exclusive private estates.

qa.q: Can I build a permanent home on an unspoiled shoreline?
qa.a: No. Permanent private homes along pristine shorelines or ecological sanctuaries are prohibited.

qa.q: How can people stay in these places?
qa.a: Temporary stays are given out by open public lottery: rotating rest stays open to all citizens, fellowships for scientists and artists, and fair public visits. No family or official may ever hold such a place permanently.

articles.article_title: Adjudication of Usufructuary Disputes and Assembly Thresholds
articles.chapter_title: PROPERTY DECONSTRUCTION & THE JURISPRUDENCE OF USUFRUCT

qa.q: Who decides local land-use and zoning changes?
qa.a: Citizens chosen by lot, in open debate. Neighborhood changes go to a council of 15 citizens; regional industrial zoning and access rights over river basins go to an assembly of 101 delegates. Both decide by a 60% majority.

qa.q: Can my right to use my land or home be taken away for public works?
qa.a: Only in extraordinary cases: 75% of the seated assembly must agree, and an equivalent home and full physical restoration must be provided first. The Local Mediation Panel must certify this unanimously.

qa.q: What if the panel refuses to certify?
qa.a: The refusal can be appealed to an independent panel of 15 citizens from other river basins.

articles.article_title: The Thermodynamic Boundary and Demonetization of the Commons
articles.chapter_title: BIOPHYSICAL REALITY & THERMODYNAMIC RESOURCE ACCOUNTING

qa.q: What is the economy based on?
qa.a: Physical laws of energy and material balance, measured in kWh of usable energy, kg of dry material, litres of clean water and regeneration cycle times.

qa.q: Does money or debt count as a claim on shared natural resources?
qa.a: No. Fiat money, compound debt and speculative pricing have no legal standing as claims on the shared natural resources.

qa.q: How much can a community use?
qa.a: No more than local watersheds and the biosphere can verifiably replenish. No production may be authorized beyond local replacement limits.

qa.q: How must basic needs like shelter and healthcare be secured?
qa.a: Each year a public audit must show local resources and installed capacity fully meet these needs, with zero external inputs and a published reserve margin.

articles.article_title: Absolute Prohibition of Usury, Speculation, and Debt Compounding
articles.chapter_title: BIOPHYSICAL REALITY & THERMODYNAMIC RESOURCE ACCOUNTING

qa.q: Are loans with compounding interest or speculative bets allowed?
qa.a: No. Any contract requiring compound interest, debt bondage or speculation on financial derivatives is void and cannot be enforced.

qa.q: What is credit for?
qa.a: Only for planning how energy, raw materials and tool time are shared out for approved public works, community upkeep or restoring nature.

qa.q: What happens if a project fails?
qa.a: You cannot be made destitute, forced into labor, or lose your right to use your home or land. Debts cannot grow, and shared resources cannot be pledged as collateral.

articles.article_title: The Three-Tier Democratic Hierarchy of Needs
articles.chapter_title: BIOPHYSICAL REALITY & THERMODYNAMIC RESOURCE ACCOUNTING

qa.q: Who gets resources first?
qa.a: Everyone's basic survival needs: clean water, food, shelter, heating and cooling, and healthcare. This comes before everything else and cannot be negotiated.

qa.q: What comes after basic needs are covered?
qa.a: Upkeep of shared infrastructure such as water treatment, power grids, public transit, communication networks and hospitals.

qa.q: How are leftover resources for creative work shared out?
qa.a: Only once the first two levels are secured. Surplus goes through preference voting and shared workshop schedules, with no price and no central office.

qa.q: Can I sell or hold on to a workshop machine slot?
qa.a: No. Slots cannot be transferred, and if unused after a short grace period they pass to waiting creators chosen by lot. Everything made on shared machines is published openly.

articles.article_title: Bioregional Carrying Capacity, Telemetry, and Analog Ground-Truthing
articles.chapter_title: BIOPHYSICAL REALITY & THERMODYNAMIC RESOURCE ACCOUNTING

qa.q: Is there a limit on how much people can take from nature and make in my area?
qa.a: Yes. Extraction and manufacturing in each watershed are limited by its Ecological Carrying Capacity.

qa.q: Can the sensors be used to watch me?
qa.a: No. Sensors may only track non-personal environmental variables. Surveillance, biometric tracking, or profiling of individual households is an absolute constitutional crime.

qa.q: Who can see what the sensors record?
qa.a: Anyone. The sensor arrays are publicly accessible, and their hardware must be open and its firmware verifiable.

qa.q: How do we know the sensors are telling the truth?
qa.a: Neighborhood Councils regularly send lay squads with manual instruments to check. Duplicate sealed samples go to independent laboratories chosen by lot from non-contiguous watersheds.

articles.article_title: Strategic Physical Reserves and Non-Linear Resilience
articles.chapter_title: BIOPHYSICAL REALITY & THERMODYNAMIC RESOURCE ACCOUNTING

qa.q: Why does each region keep emergency reserves?
qa.a: To stay resilient against disruptions, droughts, solar storms or epidemics. Each bioregional federation must maintain these reserves.

qa.q: What do the reserves have to cover?
qa.a: They must keep Tier 1 output going for 12–24 months without outside supplies, using stored goods, spare parts and backup capacity.

qa.q: Can the reserves be sold off?
qa.a: No. They cannot be sold for speculative trade, exported for external fiat, or turned into discretionary surplus.

articles.article_title: Auditing, Assembly Parity, and Decision Thresholds
articles.chapter_title: BIOPHYSICAL REALITY & THERMODYNAMIC RESOURCE ACCOUNTING

qa.q: Who checks the public accounts of physical resources?
qa.a: Randomly chosen citizens. Groups of fifteen review neighborhood utilities, and groups of 101 delegates oversee regional energy distribution and strategic reserves.

qa.q: How many votes are needed to change the basic survival allocations?
qa.a: 75%. Altering, reducing or recalculating each person's Tier 1 survival allocation requires this level.

qa.q: What majority is needed for five-year energy budgets and discretionary allocations?
Can a bare majority ever decide?
qa.a: Yes, only to release strategic reserves during certified natural disasters or ecological crises. That decision must be reviewed after thirty (30) days.

articles.article_title: The Principle of the Lot (Demarchy) and Abolition of Oligarchy
articles.chapter_title: GOVERNANCE BY LOT: THE SORTITION ARCHITECTURE

qa.q: Who makes the laws and big decisions?
qa.a: Only assemblies of citizens picked by lottery, chosen so they reflect the population.

qa.q: What happens to political parties, campaign money and lobbying?
qa.a: They are abolished, along with permanent parliamentary classes, because they let a small elite take control.

qa.q: Can groups still try to influence the people chosen by lottery?
qa.a: No. You may still join groups and speak out, but no group may finance, nominate, instruct or reward the chosen delegates. Any such act is void.

articles.article_title: Tiered Assembly Architecture and Invariant Odd Parity
articles.chapter_title: GOVERNANCE BY LOT: THE SORTITION ARCHITECTURE

qa.q: Why does every group have an odd number of members?
qa.a: To prevent ties and deadlock.

qa.q: How big are the groups?
qa.a: There are five levels, with 3, 15, 101, 301 and 1,001 citizens, from neighborhood up to the whole planet.

qa.q: Who runs a very small settlement?
qa.a: With fewer than 50 adult residents, the three-person panel runs it. Anyone party to a ruling can appeal to a panel of 15 citizens.

qa.q: When does a settlement get a larger council?
qa.a: Automatically, once it reaches fifty adult residents. A council of 15 citizens then oversees local commons, utilities and facilities.

articles.article_title: Stratified Selection, Universal Service, and Anti-Bureaucratic Rotation
articles.chapter_title: GOVERNANCE BY LOT: THE SORTITION ARCHITECTURE

qa.q: How are people chosen to serve on these panels?
qa.a: By public lottery from registers of all citizens. The draw is balanced to mirror the population by age, gender and geography.

qa.q: Can I be made to serve, and what happens to my job?
qa.a: Yes, it is a duty for everyone chosen. You are fully released from routine work, and your domestic support is replaced.

qa.q: Can I serve twice in a row?
qa.a: No. Not in the same tier consecutively; after serving you must wait twice as long as your term.

qa.q: How does a petition get onto the agenda?
qa.a: Anyone can publish one. To reach the agenda it needs endorsement from a fixed share of members, then wins a place in a public lottery.

articles.article_title: Adversarial Expert Testimony and Intelligible Decision-Making
articles.chapter_title: GOVERNANCE BY LOT: THE SORTITION ARCHITECTURE

qa.q: Who decides, the jurors or the experts?
qa.a: The jurors deliberate and decide. Technical advisors only give evidence and have no vote.

qa.q: How are complex proposals checked?
qa.a: Two rival expert panels, free from corporate grants or debt, question each other's assumptions and biases in open session.

qa.q: What if experts use technical language I can't follow?
qa.a: Experts must explain their models in plain language, including consequences, trade-offs and failure scenarios.

qa.q: What happens if the experts just create confusion or gridlock?
qa.a: Approval is withheld, but only for new structural interventions. Routine maintenance and critical life support continue. Lasting deadlocks go to a panel of scientific practitioners.

articles.article_title: Deliberative Protocols and Graduated Voting Thresholds
articles.chapter_title: GOVERNANCE BY LOT: THE SORTITION ARCHITECTURE

qa.q: How many votes does a decision need?
qa.a: It depends on the decision: 75% for the biggest changes, 60% for major plans and general rules, and 50%+1 for routine matters and emergencies.

qa.q: What happens to an emergency decision passed by a simple majority?
qa.a: It ends automatically after 30 days, with no extension. To continue, it must be approved again by 60%.

qa.q: Are percentages counted from the members who are present?
qa.a: No. They are counted from all seated members, rounded up to the next whole vote. For example, 60% of 15 members means 9 votes.

articles.article_title: Constitutional Review (*Custodes Constitutionis*)
articles.chapter_title: GOVERNANCE BY LOT: THE SORTITION ARCHITECTURE

qa.q: Who can ask for a law or decision to be checked against the Constitution?
qa.a: Any citizen, assembly, or Guardian of the Biosphere, for any law, decree, algorithm, or Organic Law they think breaks the Constitution.

qa.q: Who decides, and how?
qa.a: A jury of 101 citizens chosen by lot from regions not involved in the dispute. A 60% majority cancels the act; doubts favor the person.

qa.q: Can I appeal the result?
qa.a: Yes. Each party may appeal once to a new jury of 301 citizens.

qa.q: Can the jury rewrite the law?
qa.a: No. It can only declare that an act conforms to the Constitution or is void.

articles.article_title: Shared Maintenance, Rotational Shifts, and Ergonomic Multipliers
articles.chapter_title: ESSENTIAL PHYSICAL LABOR, CARE & INTERGENERATIONAL SURVIVAL

qa.q: Who has to do the essential maintenance work, like sanitation and harvesting?
qa.a: Able-bodied adults, in turns. Work that machines can't yet do is a shared duty, spread through rotating rosters.

qa.q: Can someone pay me to do their shift, or hire me?
qa.a: No. Human effort can't be bought, rented, traded, or forced through wage contracts or debt.

qa.q: Do dangerous jobs count for more?
qa.a: Yes. Hazardous tasks like firefighting or rescue count 3x–5x toward your duty. Standing by without active work counts at 1.0x.

qa.q: Will I have to do this work forever?
qa.a: No. The goal is full automation, and mandatory physical shifts are meant to shrink toward zero as robots take over.

articles.article_title: The Reciprocity Invariant and Anti-Free-Riding Sanctions
articles.chapter_title: ESSENTIAL PHYSICAL LABOR, CARE & INTERGENERATIONAL SURVIVAL

qa.q: Can anyone take away my water, food, housing or basic health care?
qa.a: No. These basics are yours by birth and can't be revoked or made conditional on work.

qa.q: What happens if I refuse my work shifts without a medical reason?
qa.a: Milder steps come first: a meeting with a 3-citizen panel, then loss of some advanced resources, then possibly a smaller home beyond basic shelter. No prison.

qa.q: Do I lose my political rights or keep a stigma?
qa.a: No. Voting-type rights and eligibility for selection by lot never depend on work, and the measures carry no lasting stigma.

qa.q: How do I get my access back?
qa.a: Resume any scheduled shift or agreed equivalent contribution, and full access to the restricted resources returns immediately.

articles.article_title: Empirical Child Education and Neurodevelopmental Integrity
articles.chapter_title: ESSENTIAL PHYSICAL LABOR, CARE & INTERGENERATIONAL SURVIVAL

qa.q: What is taught in schools, and what is not?
qa.a: Only methods backed by repeated scientific testing and proven teaching approaches. Passing fads, indoctrination and standardized testing groups are permanently barred.

qa.q: What do young children up to age 7 learn?
qa.a: Hands-on learning: nature, working the soil, physical shapes, live music and play that is not measured or tested.

qa.q: What happens between ages 7 and 13?
qa.a: Children are taught to spot flawed thinking, understand uncertainty and feedback, and question through dialogue so that ego does not drive inquiry.

qa.q: What happens from age 13?
qa.a: Teenagers join working research, farming and building groups alongside adult mentors, and build skill through real work reviewed by peers.

articles.article_title: Empirical Parenting Education and Universal Alloparenting
articles.chapter_title: ESSENTIAL PHYSICAL LABOR, CARE & INTERGENERATIONAL SURVIVAL

qa.q: Will there be classes on how to raise children?
qa.a: Yes. Local communities set up parenting education centres based on evidence, covering how babies bond and calm down, and working through trauma passed down in families.

qa.q: Do I have to spend time caring for other people's children?
qa.a: Yes. As a civic requirement, young adults complete practical rotations in community nurseries and childcare centres, supervised by experienced mentors, learning skills like pediatric first aid.

qa.q: What help do new parents get?
qa.a: Postpartum caregivers and child health specialists live within residential circles, guaranteeing 24-hour relief, shared meals, and full release from civic work duties for new parents.

articles.article_title: Empirical Neuro-Medicine and Etiological Mental Health
articles.chapter_title: ESSENTIAL PHYSICAL LABOR, CARE & INTERGENERATIONAL SURVIVAL

qa.q: What happens to the current way mental illness is diagnosed and treated?
qa.a: Diagnosis by symptom checklists and profit-driven lifelong sedation with drugs are permanently abolished. Mental health care relies on evidence-based neuro-medicine and diagnosis by cause.

qa.q: How is anxiety or constant stress treated?
qa.a: Mainly as the body's reaction to a stressful environment, addressed through community security, autonomy and access to nature.

qa.q: What happens if I have lasting psychiatric suffering?
qa.a: Doctors look for objective biological markers, such as brain activity and inflammation tests. Treatment favors healing approaches, and neurodiversity is never chemically blunted to make you conform.

qa.q: Can doctors decide what counts as correct treatment?
qa.a: No. No medical guild or assembly may hold a dogmatic monopoly; methods stay open to ongoing testing and open clinical review.

articles.article_title: Caregiver Immunity and Sortition Governance
articles.chapter_title: ESSENTIAL PHYSICAL LABOR, CARE & INTERGENERATIONAL SURVIVAL

qa.q: Do I have to do maintenance shifts if I care for family or community members?
qa.a: No. If you actively care for others every day, such as children or elders, you are fully exempt from rotating physical maintenance shifts.

qa.q: Who oversees the shift rosters?
qa.a: Neighborhood councils of 15 citizens, chosen by lot, supervise the rosters.

qa.q: Who can change the work multipliers or education standards?
qa.a: The regional citizen assembly of 101 delegates, by a 75% vote.

articles.article_title: The Decoupling Mandate and Thirty-Day Islanded Autonomy
articles.chapter_title: DISTRIBUTED INFRASTRUCTURE, MICROGRIDS & ANALOG RESILIENCE

qa.q: What must every community be able to do on its own?
qa.a: Run without outside help. Each community must build and keep infrastructure that lets it be fully self-sufficient when cut off.

qa.q: How long must it keep essentials going if it is cut off?
qa.a: At least 30 days in a row, covering clean water, home heating and cooling, medical refrigeration, and basic food preparation.

qa.q: Can a community rely on one distant or centralized source for its key utilities?
qa.a: No. Designs that make a key utility depend on a single outside cartel or fragile long-distance grid are unconstitutional.

articles.article_title: Modular Distributed Energy and Thermodynamic Microgrid Architecture
articles.chapter_title: DISTRIBUTED INFRASTRUCTURE, MICROGRIDS & ANALOG RESILIENCE

qa.q: Where does the power come from?
qa.a: Only renewable sources: solar panels, small water turbines, small wind generators and local biomass digestion. Generation is spread out and built in modules.

qa.q: What kind of batteries or storage are allowed?
qa.a: Non-toxic, long-lasting, fire-safe storage that doesn't depend on toxic or monopolized scarce minerals. An annex to the Organic Law lists the qualifying technologies.

qa.q: How is the power delivered?
qa.a: Locally, mostly through direct current lines linking generation, storage and heavy machinery. Alternating current is used where distance and standard machinery require it.

qa.q: What happens to big computing loads when power runs short?
qa.a: They throttle down instantly to protect Tier 1 baselines. Their waste heat is piped into district heating and greenhouses.

articles.article_title: Open Fabrication Commons and Universal Repairability
articles.chapter_title: DISTRIBUTED INFRASTRUCTURE, MICROGRIDS & ANALOG RESILIENCE

qa.q: Where can I get things made or repaired?
qa.a: At municipal fabrication commons and neighborhood workshops. Every bioregional node must keep equipped municipal workshops for farming, energy and public infrastructure.

qa.q: Can a company make its tools impossible to repair?
qa.a: No. Planned obsolescence, digital vendor locks and proprietary software on mechanical tools and spare parts are legally void.

qa.q: Can I get the plans for a machine to fix or copy it?
qa.a: Yes. Mechanical blueprints and schematics are a public commons, open to everyone for local maintenance and replication.

qa.q: What kind of control systems do machines use?
qa.a: Open-hardware controllers running transparent, auditable machine code.

articles.article_title: Distributed Telecommunications Mesh and Optical Corridors
articles.chapter_title: DISTRIBUTED INFRASTRUCTURE, MICROGRIDS & ANALOG RESILIENCE

qa.q: Who runs the communications networks?
qa.a: The population itself. Communications infrastructure is a shared, decentralized resource maintained directly by the people who use it.

qa.q: How do the public networks connect?
qa.a: Through local wireless mesh networks, line-of-sight optical links, directional relays, and license-free low-power long-range radio.

qa.q: Can anyone watch or control my traffic?
qa.a: No. Routing is self-healing and encrypted end-to-end, built to resist centralized packet inspection and corporate choke points.

qa.q: How are regions linked together?
qa.a: By high-bandwidth optical fibers along rail corridors and aqueducts, forming open backbones with no sovereign telecommunication gatekeepers.

articles.article_title: The Black-Sky Protocol and Analog Mechanical Fallbacks
articles.chapter_title: DISTRIBUTED INFRASTRUCTURE, MICROGRIDS & ANALOG RESILIENCE

qa.q: Why must water and power systems have manual backups?
qa.a: So people can survive if electronics fail, for example from electromagnetic pulses or solar storms. Essential life-support networks need controls that work without electronics.

qa.q: How must these manual controls work?
qa.a: By hand, with levers and counterweights, needing no software, electric power or remote signals. This covers water gates, sewer valves, and emergency medical storage.

qa.q: What happens to a critical facility that can't be run by hand?
qa.a: It is unconstitutional and barred from operating. The manual equipment and printed plans must also be kept and inspected at certified intervals.

qa.q: What if someone attacks life-critical systems through the network?
qa.a: Physical switches must cut the system off from outside networks instantly. It then runs on local, write-protected controllers that need no outside connection.

articles.article_title: Infrastructure Governance, Parity, and Decision Thresholds
articles.chapter_title: DISTRIBUTED INFRASTRUCTURE, MICROGRIDS & ANALOG RESILIENCE

qa.q: Who decides on local utilities and shared workshops in my neighborhood?
qa.a: A council of fifteen (15) citizens chosen by lot. They decide by a sixty percent (60%) majority.

qa.q: Who decides on big projects like regional power links, water pipelines and fiber-optic backbones?
qa.a: An assembly of one hundred and one (101) delegates for the bioregion.

qa.q: How many votes are needed for major decisions?
qa.a: 75% to shut down critical life-support assets or transfer common infrastructure. 60% for regional grid links, water treaties or five-year development plans.

qa.q: Can a bare majority ever decide?
qa.a: Only for emergencies: load shedding, protective system disconnection or immediate disaster repairs. These get an automatic review after thirty (30) days.

articles.article_title: The Axiom of Non-Sovereign Code and the Subordination of Algorithms
articles.chapter_title: OPEN COMPILER INTEGRITY & THE DEMOCRATIZATION OF CODE

qa.q: Can a computer program make decisions that bind people?
qa.a: No. Software and algorithms are only administrative tools, always under the authority of people and randomly chosen citizen assemblies.

qa.q: Can an algorithm write laws, hand down sentences, or ration resources?
qa.a: No. Handing those tasks, or any force against people, to automated systems or AI is void. Intercepting incoming unmanned machines and projectiles is not force against people.

qa.q: What kind of automation is allowed?
qa.a: Only verifiable systems with no will of their own, no legal personhood and no sovereign standing, which carry out allocations that humans decide.

articles.article_title: Absolute Prohibition of Proprietary Software in Public Commons
articles.chapter_title: OPEN COMPILER INTEGRITY & THE DEMOCRATIZATION OF CODE

qa.q: Can public services use software whose code is secret or owned by a company?
qa.a: No. Closed, hidden, proprietary or trade-secret software is permanently banned in public administration, infrastructure, manufacturing, microgrids and communication networks.

qa.q: What rules apply to the software and firmware in these systems?
qa.a: All of it, including operating systems and controller firmware, must be in the public domain, with no patents, IP claims or commercial licensing locks.

qa.q: What if a contract tries to bring proprietary software back?
qa.a: It has no legal effect. Any contract or digital lock that tries to restore proprietary software monopolies is void.

articles.article_title: Bit-for-Bit Deterministic Reproducibility and Diverse Double-Compilation (DDC)
articles.chapter_title: OPEN COMPILER INTEGRITY & THE DEMOCRATIZATION OF CODE

qa.q: What must software on public life-support systems be able to do?
qa.a: Each program must be rebuildable from its readable source code into exactly the same binary, bit for bit, to rule out hidden backdoors and spying.

qa.q: Is there an extra check for the most critical software?
qa.a: Yes. Operating system cores, encryption libraries and industrial controller firmware must be built with several independent open-source toolchains and on different processor designs.

qa.q: What happens if nobody can reproduce a program?
qa.a: It is immediately removed from public infrastructure if any citizen node cannot rebuild the same hash from the public source.

articles.article_title: Threshold Key Dispersion (t-MPC) and Non-Biometric Authentication
articles.chapter_title: OPEN COMPILER INTEGRITY & THE DEMOCRATIZATION OF CODE

qa.q: Can one person or group control the main digital keys of public networks?
qa.a: No. No engineer, programming group, regional node, or administrative council may hold sole master access over public commons networks.

qa.q: How are the most powerful keys and access protected?
qa.a: They are split into pieces held by randomly chosen, varied groups of people across several watersheds, so no single company, state, or guild can take control.

qa.q: What does it take to approve changes?
qa.a: Routine signing needs agreement among multiple nodes. Major protocol changes need a joint ceremony across the randomly chosen assemblies.

qa.q: How do I prove I'm a real person without giving up my face or identity?
qa.a: A zero-knowledge proof confirms you are one living person without collecting biometric traits, facial images, or personal identity data.

articles.article_title: The Civic De-Esotericism Mandate and Auditing of Public Algorithms
articles.chapter_title: OPEN COMPILER INTEGRITY & THE DEMOCRATIZATION OF CODE

qa.q: Why must public algorithms be documented?
qa.a: To stop a small group of unelected software experts from gaining control. Public algorithm specifications, allocation rules and compiler tools must have documentation people can read.

qa.q: Who has to show that these algorithms follow the constitution?
qa.a: Technical guilds. They must provide plain-language summaries, open-source tests and interactive sandboxes showing the algorithms meet constitutional baselines.

qa.q: What happens if an algorithm is deliberately hidden or too hard for ordinary people to understand?
qa.a: It is void and cannot run on common infrastructure. This applies if it is deliberately obscured or independent adversarial auditors prove ordinary citizens cannot understand how it works.

articles.article_title: Continuous Red-Teaming, Assembly Parity, and Decision Thresholds
articles.chapter_title: OPEN COMPILER INTEGRITY & THE DEMOCRATIZATION OF CODE

qa.q: How are security weaknesses in the digital systems found?
qa.a: Public, independent bounty programs are permanently funded and supported to keep testing the systems for vulnerabilities, hidden backdoors, and ways power could become centralized.

qa.q: Who oversees digital systems?
qa.a: Neighborhood interfaces are overseen by councils of 15 citizens. Regional code and industrial firmware standards are directed by assemblies of 101 delegates.

qa.q: How many votes are needed to decide?
qa.a: It depends: 75% to change core security standards, 60% for regional software releases, and 50%+1 only for emergencies, reviewed automatically after 30 days.

articles.article_title: Abolition of Militarized Policing, Weapon Ban, and Transitional Defense
articles.chapter_title: PUBLIC SAFETY, DEFENSIVE DETERRENCE & RESTORATIVE JUSTICE

qa.q: Can police or other civic staff keep guns and explosives?
qa.a: No. Militarized policing is permanently abolished, and civic personnel may not stockpile firearms, munitions, explosives, or neuro-irritants.

qa.q: Who keeps people safe instead?
qa.a: Unarmed peace guilds that mediate and de-escalate, and rescue and fire guilds. Rescue equipment may never be used to force people.

qa.q: Can anyone build weapons meant to hurt people?
qa.a: No. This is banned for humans and machines alike. The only exception is the temporary defense system, which may never target persons.

qa.q: Does O.N.E. have any defense at all?
qa.a: Yes, until the whole planet joins. Sealed underground platforms may automatically stop incoming projectiles and uncrewed machines, never persons or crewed vehicles, and are dismantled afterward.

articles.article_title: Ambient Spatial Safety and Non-Injurious Telemetry
articles.chapter_title: PUBLIC SAFETY, DEFENSIVE DETERRENCE & RESTORATIVE JUSTICE

qa.q: How are public spaces made safe?
qa.a: Corridors and homes keep daylight sightlines so there are no places where you could be trapped. Automated machines shut down when a person comes near.

qa.q: Do public sensors listen to or record me?
qa.a: They never record speech. They process sound only to detect impacts or structural cracks, and delete other data almost instantly.

qa.q: Can public sensors keep a record of my body data?
qa.a: No. Public sensors may never compile biometric registries.

articles.article_title: The Charter of Victims’ Sovereignty and Reparative Primacy
articles.chapter_title: PUBLIC SAFETY, DEFENSIVE DETERRENCE & RESTORATIVE JUSTICE

qa.q: Do I have to take part in a meeting with the person who harmed me?
qa.a: No. You can decline restorative dialogue, and you face no penalty for it.

qa.q: If I am hurt physically, who has to move out?
qa.a: The person who harmed you. You keep your home, and they are moved outside your transit radius.

qa.q: What help do I get first?
qa.a: Immediate trauma therapy and material restitution, both guaranteed before resources go to rehabilitating the person who harmed you.

articles.article_title: The Three-Stage Restorative Ladder and Fact-Centric Inquiry
articles.chapter_title: PUBLIC SAFETY, DEFENSIVE DETERRENCE & RESTORATIVE JUSTICE

qa.q: What happens first when I have a dispute with someone?
qa.a: You sit down with an unarmed mediator to talk and try to agree on voluntary repayment or repair for the harm.

qa.q: What if that doesn't work?
qa.a: A community circle of peers talks through the serious conflict and ends with binding agreements. After that comes a tribunal of fifteen citizens, whose decision is binding.

qa.q: What can the tribunal rule on?
qa.a: Only physical assault, bodily violation, enclosure, or ecological poisoning. Beliefs and ideas cannot be prosecuted.

qa.q: How is the evidence handled?
qa.a: There are no adversarial trials. Only verifiable physical evidence and open logs count, and forensic data must be reproducible under open review.

articles.article_title: Custodia Civilis Territorialis and Inviolable Habeas Corpus
articles.chapter_title: PUBLIC SAFETY, DEFENSIVE DETERRENCE & RESTORATIVE JUSTICE

qa.q: Will there be prisons or the death penalty?
qa.a: No. Incarceration, solitary confinement, punitive cages and execution are permanently abolished.

qa.q: What happens to someone who commits violence and doesn't calm down?
qa.a: They are restrained in a residential suite with a garden, meals and psychiatric care. Sensory deprivation, chemical blunting and punitive isolation are banned.

qa.q: How long can I be held before a group of citizens checks it?
qa.a: 72 hours. A panel of 15 randomly chosen citizens must confirm the detention by then, or you must be released.

qa.q: How often is ongoing custody reviewed?
qa.a: Every 180 days, by a newly seated jury of 15 citizens. Continuing custody needs a 60% majority.

articles.article_title: Adjudicative Assembly Parity and Decision Thresholds
articles.chapter_title: PUBLIC SAFETY, DEFENSIVE DETERRENCE & RESTORATIVE JUSTICE

qa.q: How many people decide a case?
qa.a: It depends on the level: three citizens on a Local Panel, fifteen on a Neighborhood Tribunal, and 101 delegates on a Bioregional Review Chamber.

qa.q: How big a majority is needed for a decision?
qa.a: It varies. Changing procedural protections needs 75%, and a territorial custody decree or its renewal needs 60%. A bare majority (50%+1) is allowed only for 72-hour protective detention after active violence.

qa.q: Can I leave the area if I want to?
qa.a: Yes. You can leave the bioregion freely with your personal belongings, and no one may pursue you with detention or punishment for it.

articles.article_title: The Dual-Track Handshake and Parallel Life-Support Systems
articles.chapter_title: THE TRANSITIONAL BRIDGE: FROM CAPITAL ENCLOSURE TO COMMONS

qa.q: How does the shift away from today's money-driven economy happen?
qa.a: Through a planned two-part approach called the Dual-Track Handshake, not through violent upheaval.

qa.q: What do local groups actually build?
qa.a: Open-source infrastructure, community-owned land trusts and mutual aid networks that provide life support alongside the existing market economy, which is failing under ecological and financial debt crises.

qa.q: Why would people move over to the commons?
qa.a: Because supply chains and public services fail, and the commons offers immediate, verified, reliable life support outside buying and selling, without ideological pressure.

articles.article_title: Defensive Legal Shields, Adverse Possession, and Asset Locks
articles.chapter_title: THE TRANSITIONAL BRIDGE: FROM CAPITAL ENCLOSURE TO COMMONS

qa.q: How are the commons' assets protected from being sold or seized?
qa.a: They are held in trusts that are locked permanently. They cannot be sold, mortgaged, or divided for financial gain.

qa.q: What happens to abandoned or empty land and buildings?
qa.a: They are taken into public use, through adverse possession, common heritage easements, and emergency public health declarations.

qa.q: What happens to corporate patents and trade secrets on medicines, energy designs, and tools?
qa.a: They are declared open for public use and immediately published in open-source hardware repositories.

articles.article_title: The External Trade Interface (ETI) and Demonetization Buffer
articles.chapter_title: THE TRANSITIONAL BRIDGE: FROM CAPITAL ENCLOSURE TO COMMONS

qa.q: How does the community get things it can't make locally?
qa.a: Regional groups run an External Trade Interface to buy industrial materials, specialized electronics and advanced medicines from outside, without bringing money inequality inside.

qa.q: Is money used inside the community?
qa.a: No. No official currency, speculative debt or market pricing is used within the commons.

qa.q: What happens to money earned from selling outside?
qa.a: Within 24 hours it must go into binding purchase contracts, escrow, or delivery of lasting assets, grain reserves or raw materials.

articles.article_title: Total Asymmetric Dissuasion, Defection Bounties, and Industrial Denial
articles.chapter_title: THE TRANSITIONAL BRIDGE: FROM CAPITAL ENCLOSURE TO COMMONS

qa.q: Does O.N.E. have an army?
qa.a: No. It rejects standing armies sent abroad, forced military service for offense, and hired mercenaries. It defends through civilian resistance, fortification and denying attackers supplies.

qa.q: What happens to an enemy soldier who stops fighting?
qa.a: Yes, if they lay down arms, refuse offensive orders or sabotage the attack. They get asylum, lifelong basic security, housing, and cancellation of their family's external debts.

qa.q: What happens to captured or surrendered weapons?
qa.a: They are permanently dismantled and melted in public foundries. The metal becomes wind turbine shafts, farm tools and building frames.

qa.q: What if invaders occupy the territory anyway?
qa.a: Randomly selected officials cut the security keys, permanently disabling advanced industry and computing. Basic domestic water and heating keep running.

articles.article_title: Universal Debt Jubilees and Insolvent Asset Transformation
articles.chapter_title: THE TRANSITIONAL BRIDGE: FROM CAPITAL ENCLOSURE TO COMMONS

qa.q: What happens to failed factories, shipping hubs and utility networks?
qa.a: They are taken over by local community trusts (called municipal commons trusts).

qa.q: What happens to my debts?
qa.a: Compound-interest debts, predatory home mortgages and financial liens held by older institutions against homes and life-support systems are cancelled.

qa.q: What is done with the taken-over factories?
qa.a: They are rebuilt with open-source controllers and modular machine tools for metal recycling, farm machinery repair and local public utility.

articles.article_title: Transitional Governance, Assembly Parity, and Decision Thresholds
articles.chapter_title: THE TRANSITIONAL BRIDGE: FROM CAPITAL ENCLOSURE TO COMMONS

qa.q: Who runs the legal trusts, outside trade and the move between phases?
qa.a: Randomly chosen groups of people: panels of 3, councils of 15 and regional assemblies of 101, all working in the open.

qa.q: How many votes are needed for the biggest decisions?
qa.a: 75%. This covers cancelling all debts, forcing industrial assets to be converted, and approving a move to the next phase.

qa.q: What about trade budgets and agreements with neighbors?
qa.a: 60% is needed for yearly trade budgets and regional mutual-aid agreements with adjacent transitional nodes.

qa.q: When is a bare majority enough?
qa.a: Only for non-lethal defensive blocking and quick supply changes during an emergency embargo, followed by a required review within thirty (30) days.

articles.article_title: The Watershed as Primary Sovereign Unit and Bioregional Subsidiarity
articles.chapter_title: BIOREGIONAL WATERSHED FEDERATION & THE PLANETARY COVENANT

qa.q: Do countries and national borders still exist?
qa.a: No. National borders, colonial borders and closed-off sovereign territories are permanently abolished.

qa.q: What replaces them as the basic unit of government?
qa.a: The natural watershed: an area defined by its water catchments, underground water supplies and coastal ecosystems.

qa.q: Who makes decisions?
qa.a: The smallest local level that can handle the matter, from neighborhood water basins up to valley councils.

qa.q: Can higher assemblies overrule local decisions?
qa.a: Only to stop pollution sent elsewhere, protect shared underground water, or defend rights that cannot be changed.

articles.article_title: Ecological Personhood and Interspecies Guardianship (*Jus Biosphaerae*)
articles.chapter_title: BIOREGIONAL WATERSHED FEDERATION & THE PLANETARY COVENANT

qa.q: Can a river or forest be owned or sold?
qa.a: No. Major rivers, ancient forests, coastal wetlands and aquifers cannot be owned, leased or turned into goods. They count as legal persons with a right to exist and regenerate.

qa.q: Who speaks for nature when decisions are made?
qa.a: Guardians, made up of citizens chosen by lot and rotating field naturalists. They represent natural areas and future generations in all assemblies.

qa.q: Can anyone stop a project that harms nature?
qa.a: Yes. The Guardians can go to court to stop projects that threaten ecological continuity.

articles.article_title: Physical Inter-Basin Reciprocity and Anti-Cartel Pacts
articles.chapter_title: BIOREGIONAL WATERSHED FEDERATION & THE PLANETARY COVENANT

qa.q: How do different regions trade with each other?
qa.a: Directly, through two-party agreements to swap physical resources. No financial speculation, debt or currency exchange is involved.

qa.q: What do cities contribute in this trade?
qa.a: Advanced industrial products and scientific research, which they trade for food and energy surpluses.

qa.q: What happens if a region hoards essentials, forms a cartel, or cuts off downstream water?
qa.a: Its links to other regions are suspended immediately: power grid connections, transit routes and advanced medical support, until fair exchange is restored.

articles.article_title: Thermodynamic Freedom of Movement and Non-Coercive Carrying Capacity
articles.chapter_title: BIOREGIONAL WATERSHED FEDERATION & THE PLANETARY COVENANT

qa.q: Can I travel or move to another place freely?
qa.a: Yes. Everyone has a right to travel, visit and seek refuge. Passports, border fences, visa checkpoints and armed border patrols are banned.

qa.q: Can I always settle permanently wherever I like?
qa.a: Not always. Permanent residence depends on an area's environmental capacity: open when there is room, prioritized for some people when near its limit, and paused when full.

qa.q: What happens to me if the area I arrive in is full?
qa.a: You can't be pushed back, blocked or deported. You still get shelter, clean water, food, emergency medical care and safe transit.

qa.q: Who helps when too many people arrive in one area?
qa.a: Neighboring areas with room must send aid. If local services are overwhelmed, fast trains and ships carry arrivals past the full area to reception points in nearby areas.

articles.article_title: Planetary Commons Stewardship and Solar Flux Regulation
articles.chapter_title: BIOREGIONAL WATERSHED FEDERATION & THE PLANETARY COVENANT

qa.q: Who owns the air, oceans, ice and radio waves?
qa.a: Everyone. They are treated as shared life-support heritage of all living things, and cannot be divided up.

qa.q: Can anyone spray chemicals into the sky or sea to cool the planet?
qa.a: No. Aerosol injection, sulfur dispersal and chemical ocean fertilization are permanently banned as dangerous to the environment.

qa.q: Can anything be done about the sun's heat without chemicals?
qa.a: Yes, a reversible, non-chemical system in deep space, if 75% of the 1,001-delegate Global Commons Assembly and a majority of Continental Governance Chambers (60% each) agree.

qa.q: What happens if such a system loses its authorization or control?
qa.a: It must disperse gradually over several years set by Organic Law, never abruptly.

articles.article_title: The Federated Sortition Architecture, Odd Parity, and the Universal Covenant
articles.chapter_title: BIOREGIONAL WATERSHED FEDERATION & THE PLANETARY COVENANT

qa.q: How many people sit in the groups that make decisions?
qa.a: It depends on the level: 3 in local panels, 15 in neighborhood councils, 101 in regional assemblies, 301 in continental chambers, and 1,001 in the global assembly.

qa.q: How many votes are needed to decide something?
qa.a: It depends on the matter: 75% for the biggest changes, 60% for shared resource and infrastructure deals, and 50%+1 only for emergency relief and transit schedules.

qa.q: Can a simple majority decision stand forever?
qa.a: No. Decisions made by simple majority must be reviewed after thirty (30) days.

qa.q: Can detailed technical rules weaken the constitution?
qa.a: No. They are set by a 60% majority of the competent assembly and may only strengthen guarantees, never weaken them.

articles.article_title: The Sol Commons and Abolition of Celestial Dominium (*Patrimonium Solis*)
articles.chapter_title: THE CELESTIAL COMMONS & INTERPLANETARY FEDERATION

qa.q: Who owns space, the planets and asteroids?
qa.a: No one. Outer space, celestial bodies, asteroids, comets and orbital paths are a shared commons that cannot be divided up.

qa.q: Can a country or company claim a piece of space?
qa.a: No. National annexation, corporate sovereignty, private ownership claims and reserving celestial bodies or orbital slots are permanently barred.

qa.q: How do I get a good spot in space, like a useful orbit?
qa.a: Those spots can never be leased, sold or hoarded. Access goes through open random-draw lists and physical docking queues.

qa.q: Can I keep minerals I extract?
qa.a: Only as a right to use them, and only while you actively look after the site and immediately publish your assay results and process tooling openly.

articles.article_title: Engineered Metabolic Envelopes and Closed-Loop Carrying Capacity
articles.chapter_title: THE CELESTIAL COMMONS & INTERPLANETARY FEDERATION

qa.q: Where does the basic unit of civilization shift away from nature?
qa.a: Beyond Earth's biosphere, it moves from the natural river basin to an artificial, sealed life-support system built to sustain people.

qa.q: What happens to water, nitrogen, carbon and phosphorus in such a habitat?
qa.a: They are closed, unalterable community trusts. The habitat cannot go beyond what it has, since mass balance is an absolute limit.

qa.q: How is the number of people a habitat can hold judged?
qa.a: By how well it recirculates resources, how little it leaks, its pressure integrity and heat-shedding capacity. Permits and expansion must match a verifiable balance.

articles.article_title: Invariant Atmospheric Sovereignty and the Anti-Despotism Interlock
articles.chapter_title: THE CELESTIAL COMMONS & INTERPLANETARY FEDERATION

qa.q: What basic things am I guaranteed in a sealed habitat or ship?
qa.a: Breathable air, drinkable water, protection from radiation and temperature control. These survival rights cannot be taken away.

qa.q: Can anyone charge me for air or make me work for it?
qa.a: No. Life support cannot be sold, metered against work, or used to force obedience.

qa.q: Can software or a vote cut off my life support?
qa.a: No. Manual overrides and bypass lines must be reachable by everyone, and no program, decree or vote may throttle life support.

qa.q: Can I be put out into vacuum or have my air rationed as a penalty?
qa.a: No. Dispute measures may only suspend optional tools or computing bandwidth, never expel you, confine you in harmful ways, or ration air.

articles.article_title: Thermodynamic Astrodynamics: Mass, Exergy, and Velocity Budgets
articles.chapter_title: THE CELESTIAL COMMONS & INTERPLANETARY FEDERATION

qa.q: What is used to pay for trade and transport between planets?
qa.a: Not money or debt. Exchanges are coordinated directly by physical quantities: energy, dry mass, volatiles (liquids and gases) and velocity change.

qa.q: Is rocket fuel treated as something anyone can use freely?
qa.a: It is treated as a limited shared resource. Moving mass out of a planet's gravity costs energy, which must be balanced by proven benefit to the network.

qa.q: Who owns the big industrial refineries?
qa.a: They are held together as shared assets, in collective trust, so that no single bottleneck can disrupt supply.

articles.article_title: Light-Cone Subsidiarity and Asynchronous Demarchic Sortition
articles.chapter_title: THE CELESTIAL COMMONS & INTERPLANETARY FEDERATION

qa.q: Why isn't there one government for all of space?
qa.a: Light takes too long to cross huge distances, so one central democracy is physically impossible. Decisions that can be settled locally are not made by remote assemblies.

qa.q: Who runs daily life in a single habitat?
qa.a: A council of 15 to 101 citizens has full say over life inside, including workshop access, layout and shift coordination.

qa.q: What does the 1,001-member assembly do?
qa.a: It meets in 90-day cycles and looks after the basic rules for everyone, shared open tools, seed banks and collision avoidance.

articles.article_title: Kinetic Non-Aggression, the Orbital Immune System, and Swords into Plowshares
articles.chapter_title: THE CELESTIAL COMMONS & INTERPLANETARY FEDERATION

qa.q: Can anyone fly a spacecraft or asteroid toward a populated habitat or Earth on purpose?
qa.a: No. Deliberate propulsion burns toward inhabited habitats, moons or Earth are prohibited, because heavy moving mass works as a weapon.

qa.q: How is the Federation protected from asteroids and collisions without an army?
qa.a: It keeps spread-out interception equipment that does civilian jobs in peacetime, such as propulsion and clearing orbital debris. Beam emitters have a hardware cutoff when aimed at inhabited places.

qa.q: What happens to old propulsion stages and hulls?
qa.a: They go to foundries to be remelted into ordinary habitat rings and heat radiators. Planetary trajectories are checked by networks of optical and radar trackers.
